title: Ines and the Contact
premise: Noor Kavanagh, a crash investigator whose family died in row twelve of Flight 4471, has spent five years buried in bureaucratic routine, following safety protocols that keep being quietly rewritten by someone above them. When a routine voiceprint analysis unlocks an encrypted server in Lisbon, Noor discovers Meridian Group, a private consultancy that engineers 'accidents' to reshape markets and policy—and finds their own family's crash on the list. As Noor goes off-grid to trace the network from Lisbon to Geneva to a decommissioned airfield, they are hunted by both Meridian's fixers and the agency colleagues they once trusted. In the end, Noor exposes the pattern by forcing Meridian to trigger its next staged disaster early, in front of hundreds of witnesses, sacrificing their anonymity forever but finally giving row twelve its truth.
about_author: Marguerite Whitlock is a former aviation insurance analyst who spent a decade reading accident reports before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about the people who live inside systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Five years after losing their family on Flight 4471, Noor works night shifts re-reading black-box transcripts for the Safety Bureau, keeping everyone at arm's length. A new directive orders old case files purged—including 4471. Emotional beat: grief managed through procedure begins to crack.

chapters.title: The Voice That Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Running a final archive pass, Noor's voiceprint authentication tool flags an anomaly: a synthetic voice matching a dead pilot's cadence unlocking a server pinged from Lisbon. Against protocol, Noor copies the handshake data. Beat: curiosity overriding fear—the first rule broken.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The copied key decrypts fragments: invoices, flight manifests, and the name Meridian Group. Noor finds 4471 listed as 'Delivery 9'—the crash was commissioned. Beat: vertigo; the wound reopens as evidence.

chapters.title: Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor cross-checks five other 'accidents' against Meridian's timestamps—all match. Their supervisor, Amara Osei, notices the unauthorized access and warns Noor to drop it, then quietly slips them a burner number. Beat: the system is not neutral; an unexpected ally appears.

chapters.title: Lisbon
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Using leave days, Noor flies to Lisbon and physically locates the server in a co-working shell company. They photograph a courier exchange and recognize a face from the Bureau's own training materials. Beat: the conspiracy reaches inside the institution Noor trusted.

chapters.title: The Courier
chapters.summary: POV Tomas Ribeiro, a Meridian logistics man who is starting to ask what he ships. He delivers a drive to a woman called Voss and notices his own movements logged like cargo. Beat: complicity and unease; the enemy gets a human face.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Back home, Noor's clearance is suspended pending an integrity review—Meridian has framed them. Their apartment is searched while they watch from across the street. Beat: invisibility was never protection; the hunter becomes the hunted.

chapters.title: Amara's Number
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor calls the burner. Amara reveals she lost her brother in one of Meridian's earlier deliveries and has been collecting quietly for years. They agree to pool evidence—but she insists on rules Noor no longer believes in. Beat: belonging offered, cautiously accepted.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: POV Elena Voss, Meridian's operations director. She reviews the Lisbon breach, identifies Noor, and argues internally that Noor should be recruited, not removed—their grief makes them predictable. Beat: chilling elegance of power; corruption as management style.

chapters.title: Geneva
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Following money trails, Noor and Amara reach Geneva, where a Meridian board meeting coincides with a global aviation summit. Noor poses as an insurance adjuster and photographs the attendee list. Beat: adrenaline and impostor terror; Noor wears a false identity and feels disturbingly free.

chapters.title: What Voss Saw
chapters.summary: POV Voss. Voss discovers the board plans 'Delivery 14'—a midair failure over the Atlantic timed to kill a rival regulator's reform treaty. She realizes she is disposable too. Beat: the corrupted begin to see the machine's teeth.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Meridian's fixer, Hale, corners Noor in a hotel bar with an offer: full truth about row twelve, sealed and official, in exchange for walking away. Noor asks one question—who signed Delivery 9—and walks out when Hale smiles. Beat: temptation met and refused; identity chosen over comfort.

chapters.title: Amara Down
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Amara is hit by a car outside her flat; she survives but the evidence drive is gone. From her hospital bed she gives Noor the last backup location and tells them to finish it alone. Beat: cost made flesh; guilt and resolve fused.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Off-grid in a safehouse, Noor reconstructs Delivery 14's target: a charter flight out of a decommissioned airfield in the Azores, scheduled in nine days, engineered to look like fatigue cracking. Beat: cold clarity; the shape of the endgame emerges.

chapters.title: Tomas's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Tomas. Ordered to prep the Azores logistics, Tomas finds his name on a post-operation disposal list. He contacts Noor through the courier channel, offering the ground crew roster. Beat: a small man's defection; power corrupts even its errand runners into rebels.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Noor tries going through channels—Bureau, press, police—and watches each door close within hours, proof of Meridian's reach. Only one path remains: be inside the event when it happens. Beat: despair transmuted into strategy.

chapters.title: Infiltration
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Posing as contracted maintenance staff, Noor infiltrates the airfield with Tomas's credentials and finds the rigged component in bay three, serial-matched to parts from 4471. Beat: the past literally built into the future crime; fury sharpened to purpose.

chapters.title: Hale
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Hale catches Noor in the hangar. Instead of killing them, he reveals the final cruelty: the pilot scheduled for Delivery 14 is coerced, and Noor's exposure would only let Meridian reschedule cleaner. Noor stalls him long enough to broadcast the hangar feed. Beat: the trap within the trap; witness as weapon.

chapters.title: Delivery Fourteen
chapters.summary: POV alternating Noor/Voss. With regulators, journalists, and Amara's contacts watching the livestream, Meridian must abort or detonate in public. Voss, choosing at last, kills the triggering signal from inside and walks out to surrender herself. The flight lands safely. Beat: climax—corruption devours itself in daylight.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Hearings, arrests, and a leaked ledger dismantle Meridian. Noor testifies under their own name for the first time in years, naming Delivery 9 aloud. Beat: identity reclaimed through public truth-telling.

chapters.title: What the Recorder Kept
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The reopened 4471 file returns the cockpit recording the purge order buried. Noor listens once, at home, lights off, and lets themselves weep for row twelve. Beat: mourning finally permitted; closure without erasure.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Months later, Noor takes a teaching post training new investigators, refusing the quiet desk they once hid behind. A student asks why they stayed in the work after everything. Noor answers: because invisible people are the easiest to erase. Beat: belonging found not in hiding, but in standing seen.
